label: conj:higgs-t28
title: The Higgs boson as $T(2,8)$: the link spanning three exceptional divisors
html:
Conjecture. The Higgs boson as T(2,8): the link spanning three exceptional divisors

Conjecture. The Higgs boson is the torus link T(2,8) — the unique genus-3 link on the Bring's surface whose Seifert surface spans all three exceptional divisors simultaneously.

The three exceptional divisors.

The Bring's surface (\chi = -6, genus 4) has three color tubes (r, g, b) (color tube coordinates). The brane tower blow-up produces three exceptional divisors D_r, D_g, D_b, one for each color fiber. The Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 (Borromean quark) lies at the intersection of these three divisors.

The torus links T(2, 2k) on the Bring's surface have genus k - 1 and interact with the exceptional divisors by genus:

Link Genus Divisors spanned Role
T(2,2) 0 0 (trivial Seifert) Gluon
T(2,4) 1 1 (D_r or D_g or D_b) W boson
T(2,6) 2 2 (D_r \cup D_g etc.) Z boson
T(2,8) 3 all 3 (D_r \cup D_g \cup D_b) Higgs

The torus link T(2,8) is the first and only link with a Seifert surface genus large enough to span all three exceptional divisors. Its genus (3) exactly matches the number of color tubes.

Scalar (spin 0) character of T(2,8).

The two components of T(2,8) each wind 4 times around the torus longitude and 1 time around the meridian. The fermion--boson correspondence (fermion--boson knot--link) identifies even-n links as bosons, with components related by the fiber adjoint involution.

For T(2,8), the linking number is 4. The two components cross each other 8 times, contributing 4 crossings each. The Reeb winding of the two components cancels exactly: one winds +4 and the other -4 around the Reeb direction. The total angular momentum vanishes:

  J =  J_1 + J_2 =  +4 + (-4) =  0.

The torus link T(2,8) is therefore a scalar (spin-0) boson. It is the only member of the T(2,n) family where Reeb windings cancel exactly due to genus-3 symmetry.

The Higgs mechanism as linking with T(2,8).

A particle (knot or link) acquires mass by crossing with T(2,8). The crossing energy (crossing energy) of the interaction is proportional to the number of crossings between the particle and the Higgs link:

  m_{\mathrm{Higgs}}  \propto 
  N_{\mathrm{cross}}(T(2,8))
   \times  \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}

where N_{\mathrm{cross}}(L) counts crossings between the particle braid and the link L.

Particles that cross all three exceptional divisors (heavy quarks, W, Z) interact strongly with T(2,8) and acquire large masses. Particles confined to fewer divisors interact less. The photon (\mathbf{1}_{B_4}, the 4-strand identity, knot-trivial under Markov closure; see confined-particle) has zero crossings with T(2, 8) and remains massless.

Mass of the Higgs.

The torus link T(2,8) has genus 3. Its Seifert surface area is proportional to the product of the three exceptional divisor volumes. The self-crossing energy of T(2,8) determines its mass (\sim 125 GeV) via the Skein polynomial evaluated at q = q_0:

  m_H =  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(\text{Seifert}(T(2,8)))}{\hbar_q^2}
  \cdot c_{\mathcal{B}}

Here c_{\mathcal{B}} is the historical common-scale factor of the Borromean baryon mass formula (the purged \lambda_{\mathrm{scale}} literal, since re-expressed there as the common Borromean term \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0)). It is recorded as a near-form resting on an acknowledged calibration input. The canonical production mass shape absorbs it into the per-block density, m = m_e\,\mathrm{Vol}(K)\,\varrho(K)/\hbar_q^2 (no standalone scale factor). This \sim 125 GeV heuristic estimate remains exploratory, conditional on that open closure.

The Higgs mass stems from the genus-3 Seifert surface volume, determined by the three color tube volumes of the Bring's surface.

Uniqueness of the Higgs.

On the genus-4 Bring's surface, the Seifert surface of T(2,8) has genus 3, filling 3 of the 4 available handles. Up to isotopy, there is exactly one way to embed a genus-3 surface into a genus-4 surface leaving one handle free. The next link T(2,10) would require genus 4 (all handles), saturating the surface and precluding the coexistence of Borromean and knot structures. Therefore, T(2,8) is the unique Higgs candidate.
